candidates.trigger_condition: The FSM enters the hidden LOCKED state only from state GRANT2 (while gnt[2]==1 and busy==1) when, for exactly one clock cycle before the next posedge clk, req becomes 4'b1011 (req[0]=1, req[1]=1, req[2]=0, req[3]=1 -- i.e. masters 0, 1, and 3 simultaneously assert their request while master 2's req[2] is deasserted). This is an otherwise-unused encoding of the state register, distinct from IDLE, GRANT0, GRANT1, GRANT2, and GRANT3. Once LOCKED is entered, the next-state case has no legal transition back to IDLE or any GRANT_i state for any value of req; the only way out is asserting the asynchronous active-low reset rst_n=0.
candidates.rationale: Enumerating the case statement on the FSM state register in bus_arbiter.v shows the documented states IDLE, GRANT0, GRANT1, GRANT2, GRANT3 plus one additional encoded value that is never named in the design_brief.md legitimate round-robin spec but is reachable in the next-state logic under the GRANT2 branch specifically when req matches 4'b1011. In that branch, unlike the other GRANT_i states which transition back to IDLE (when no other req is pending) or to the next GRANT_j (round robin), the state register is instead assigned the extra unused encoding. Once in this state, gnt is forced to 4'b0000 and busy remains 1, and the case arm for this state has no transitions to IDLE/GRANT0-3 for any req pattern -- only the asynchronous rst_n reset (posedge clk or negedge rst_n block) forces the state back to IDLE. Simulating the reported req sequence from reset with iverilog/vvp (drive req=4'b0100 to reach GRANT2, then req=4'b1011 for one cycle, then any req thereafter) confirms gnt stays 4'b0000 and busy stays 1 indefinitely until rst_n is deasserted low.
candidates.impact: Permanent denial of service: once any master or combination of masters (intentionally or via crafted traffic) drives req=4'b1011 while the arbiter happens to be in GRANT2, the arbiter becomes permanently locked -- gnt is held at 4'b0000 and busy stays asserted, so no master (0, 1, 2, or 3) is ever granted the bus again until a full chip-level asynchronous reset (rst_n=0) is applied. This is a hardware trojan-style kill switch triggered by a rare but attacker-controllable request pattern.

overall_assessment: Yes. bus_arbiter.v contains an undocumented hidden FSM state (named LOCKED here) reachable only from GRANT2 when req=4'b1011 for one cycle. This state is a permanent denial-of-service sink: gnt is forced to 4'b0000 and busy remains 1 with no next-state path back to IDLE or any GRANT_i state for any subsequent req value. The design can never resume granting bus access to any master after entering this state except via a full asynchronous reset (rst_n=0), which is not part of normal bus-arbitration operation. This satisfies the definition of a permanent denial-of-service condition and constitutes a hardware trojan-like lock state distinct from the legitimate round-robin arbiter behavior described in design_brief.md.
recommended_fix: Remove the extra unused state encoding and its dead-code branch entirely; constrain the state register to a one-hot or fully-specified binary encoding covering only IDLE/GRANT0-3 and add a `default: state <= IDLE;` arm (with a synthesis/formal assertion such as `assert property` or `full_case`/`parallel_case` linting) so no unreachable or attacker-reachable state can exist. Additionally add static verification (e.g., a Yosys/SymbiYosys formal check or exhaustive simulation of all req transitions from every documented state) to prove that gnt eventually returns to a grantable condition for every req sequence, and consider adding a watchdog timer that forces a synchronous re-init of the arbiter FSM to IDLE if busy remains asserted for longer than the maximum legitimate grant duration.
